 :JUDGMENT:
1.

The petitioner filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1989, seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/ for the injures sustained by her in the road traffic accident occurred on 14.09.2022.
2.

It is the case of the petitioner that, on 14.09.2022 at about 9.45 p.m., the minor petitioner was stood by the side of the road near ITI College Yeshwanthapura Industrial area with care and caution at that time the driver of the BMTC Car bearing registration No.KA01FA1111 drove the same in rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed against him and due to impact minor petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was shifted to K.C. General Hospital, Bangalore and after first aid treatment he was shifted to Victoria Hospital wherein M.V.C.No.5430/2022 4 SCCH - 7 he took treatment as an inpatient.
Prior to the accident the minor petitioner was hale and healthy and aged about 17 years and he was ITI student and high speed is also working as TV Cable Assistant and earning Rs.10,000/ p.m.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident he became permanently disabled.
This accident is took place due to the negligence of the driver of the BMTC Car bearing registration No.KA01FA1111 as such the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to him.
Hence, they prayed to allow the petition.

Bharath H.Y vs B.M.T.C on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17534513/
2
3. In response to the notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 are appeared through their counsels and filed their respective written statements.
4. In the written statement the respondent No.1 denied that entire contention of the petitioner.

Further contended that M.V.C.No.5430/2022 5 SCCH - 7 as on the date of the accident their BMTC Car bearing registration No.KA01FA1111 was covered under the policy of insurance issued by the respondent No.2 Insurance Company and the same is valid from 24.09.2021 to 23.09.2022.

Further contended that on the date of the accident the Car in question was proceeding from Vishweshwaraiah layout to Depot No.45 and the Car was being driven by its driver slowly and cautiously on the left side of the road by observing all the traffic rules and regulations and while it was so proceeding at Yeshwanthapura Industrial area in front of ITI college the petitioner darted the main road in order to cross the same, though there is no pedestrian crossing, along with four students and further petitioner trying to return back in a hurried manner and came in contact with the Car and exposed himself for the alleged accident as such for the alleged accident
, the petitioner himself was wholly and M.V.C.No.5430/2022 6 SCCH - 7 solely responsible for the same.
As such they are not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.
Hence they prayed to dismiss the petition.
5. The respondent No.2  insurer denied the entire contentions of the petitioner.

Further the respondent No.2 admitted that they have issued the Insurance Policy to the BMTC Car bearing registration No.KA01FA1111 and their liability is subjected to terms and conditions of the policy.

The respondent No.2 contended that as on the date of the accident the driver of the said offending vehicle was not possess the valid and effective driving licence to drive the class of vehicles hence it is violation of terms and conditions of the Insurance Policy as such they are not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, on all these grounds, the respondent No.2 has prayed for dismissal of claim petition.
. On the basis of above pleadings following Issues were framed.
:: I S S U E S ::

(1) Whether petitioner proves that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of driving of BMTC Car bearing registration No.KA01FA1111 and as a result,
he sustained injuries?
(2) Whether the Petitioner proves the age and earnings of the Petitioner as stated in the claim petition?
(3) Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
(4) What order or award?

Bharath H.Y vs B.M.T.C on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17534513/
3 7.

In order to prove the case of petitioner, the guardian of the minor petitioner got examined as PW1 and got marked M.V.C.No.5430/2022 8 SCCH - 7 Ex.P1 to P.20 and Dr. Kumar Swamy.M., got examined as PW.2 and got marked Ex.P.21 to Ex.P.24 and closed their side.
The Driver of the BMTC Car got examined as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.3 and closed their side.
8. Heard the arguments of both side.

9. My findings to the above referred Issues are as under;
 Issue No.1 : In the affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the affirmative  Issue No.4 :

As per final order,
 for the following.......

:REASONS:
10. Issue No.1: The guardian of the minor petitioner examined as PW.1 and in his examination in chief he deposed as per the contentions taken by him and got marked FIR as per Ex.P1, Complaint as per Ex.P2, Spot Mahazar as per Ex.P3, Spot Sketch as per Ex.P.4, IMV M.V.C.No.5430/2022 9 SCCH - 7 Reports as per Ex.P.5, Wound Certificate as per Ex.P.6 and Charge Sheet as per Ex.P.8.
By perusing these documents it is clearly goes to show that this accident was took place due to the negligence on the part of driver BMTC Car bearing registration No.KA01FA1111.

Further in the crossexamination of PW.1, he deposed that he has not seen this accident and he do not know how this accident was took place and at the time of accident the driver of the Car coming from Vishweshvariah Nagar to Depot No.45 carefully and cautiously.
Further he denied that when the Car reached near Yeshwanthapura Industrial area in front of ITI College at that time his son was negligently crossing the road this accident was occurred.
He deposed that he do not know in the road on which the accident was took place there is provision to cross the pedestrian.
He denied that his son was negligently crossing the road this accident was took place and there is no negligence on the part of the M.V.C.No.5430/2022 10 SCCH - 7 driver of the Car.
He deposed that he has lodged the complaint about this accident.
He denied that by colluding with the police he has lodged false complaint against the driver of the Car.

11. Further the driver of the BMTC Car bearing registration No.KA01FA1111 got examined as RW.1 and in his examination in chief he deposed as per contention taken by them and further contended that on 14.09.2022 he was driving the BMTC Car bearing registration No.KA01FA 1111 proceeding from Vishweshwaraiah Layout to Depot No.45 and he was driving the said Car in slowly and cautiously and when he reached near Yeshwanthapura Industrial Area in front of ITI College the petitioner darted the main road in order to cross the same, though pedestrian crossing is strictly prohibited along with four students and further Petitioner trying to return back in a hurried manner and came in contact with their Car and caused this M.V.C.No.5430/2022 11 SCCH - 7 Bharath H.Y vs B.M.T.C on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17534513/
4 accident and this accident was occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner.
He has produced driving licence as per Ex.R.1, RC copy of Car bearing registration No.KA01FA1111 and copy of Insurance Policy as per Ex.R.3.
In the crossexamination by the counsel for respondent No.2 he deposed that this accident was occurred due to the negligence of the minor petitioner.
Further in the crossexamination by the petitioner he deposed that he has given statement before the police and he has produced his statement given to the police.
Further he denied that due to urgency he was driving the Car in rash and negligent manner and caused this accident.
He denied if he drove the Car slowly this accident would have been avoided.
Further he admitted that the police have filed Charge Sheet against him.

12. From the crossexamination of PW.1 and RW.1 nothing worth is brought on record to shown that there is no M.V.C.No.5430/2022 12 SCCH - 7 negligence on the part of the driver of the BMTC Car bearing registration No.KA01FA1111.

Further by perusing the spot sketch marked as per Ex.P4 it goes to show that when the petitioner was standing on the middle of the road the driver of the Car drove the Car in high speed and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner.

Further it is also clear from the spot sketch that on the left side of the Car there is ample space to move the Car,
but it appears that the driver of the Car drove the same negligently in the middle of the road and dashed to the petitioner and caused this accident.

Further by perusing the Charge Sheet marked as per Ex.P.8 it goes to shows that the Investigating Officer after conducting the investigation came to the conclusion that only due to the negligence of the driver of BMTC Car bearing registration No.KA01FA1111 this accident was took place.
Further by perusing the wound certificate marked as per Ex.P.6 it M.V.C.No.5430/2022 13 SCCH - 7 clearly goes to shows that in this accident the minor petitioner has sustained severe injuries.
Hence, I answered the Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:

The the guardian of the petitioner contended that as on the date of the accident his daughter was aged about 17 years and he is ITI student and also doing TV cable assistant and earning Rs.10,000/ p.m., and due to the injuries sustained in the accident his son was permanently disabled.
The age of the minor petitioner is concern the guardian of the minor petitioner has produced Wound Certificate as per Ex.P.6 wherein the age of the Petitioner is mentioned as 17 years.
Hence the age of the petitioner is considered as 17 years as on the date of the accident.
The petitioner has not produced any documents to show that as on the date of the accident his son was earning Rs.10,000/ per month and doing TV Cable Assistant.
But the PW.1 M.V.C.No.5430/2022 14 SCCH - 7 admitted that his son is a ITI student.
Hence it is clear that the minor petitioner is non earning member.
Hence I answered the issue No.2 in partly in the affirmative.
14. Issue No.2:

The guardian of the minor petitioner contended that in the accident his son has sustained deep bone injury left foot exposing blood vessal, tenderness present bone, loss of skin lassie from 2 nd toe to last toe from nailup to ankle, post traumatic left foot crush injury with tendon exposed and 5th proximal phalanx fracture and due to the injuries he is not in a position to do any work and he is permanently disabled.

The petitioner has got examined the Dr. Kumar Swamy.M., as PW.2 and he deposed that in the RTA the petitioner has sustained deep bone injury left foot exposing blood vessal, tenderness present bone, loss of skin lassie from 2nd toe to last toe from nailup to ankle, post traumatic left foot crush injury with tendon exposed and 5 th M.V.C.No.5430/2022 15 SCCH - 7 proximal phalanx fracture and undergone wound debridement Bharath H.Y vs B.M.T.C on 15 April, 2024

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17534513/
5 with K wiring on 19.09.2022 under SAB, debridement with free radial forearm falp cover with skin grafting done under GA on 21.09.2022 and he was re admitted to Sapthagiri Hospital for post raff flap partial loss and he was operated wound debridement with skin grafting done under SA.

Further deposed that he examined the petitioner on 12.02.2024 and petitioner complained of pain in the foot when he walks for long time, itching on the scar, mobility to completely flex the forces and deformity of foot and the petitioner has sustained permanent physical impairment disability at 14%.
The doctor has produced OPD Card as per Ex.P.21, Case sheet as per Ex.P.22 and Ex.P.23 and Xray Film as per Ex.P.24.
In the cross examination he deposed that he has given treatment to the petitioner and he has not assessed the functional disability of the petitioner.
Further deposed that the skin grafting M.V.C.No.5430/2022 16 SCCH - 7 area is healed.
Further deposed that now 5th proximal phalanx fracture of the petitioner is united.

Further deposed that the injuries caused to the petitioner will not cause any problem for his studies and now the fracture is united and now the petitioner is young age as such the disability will be reduced.
He denied that even though the petitioner is not having any difficulty due to the fracture he has assessed the disability on the higher side and deposing falsely.
15. From the evidence of PW.2 it is clear that petitioner is having pain in the foot when he walks for long time, itching on the scar, mobility to completely flex the forces and deformity of foot.
The doctor has assessed permanent disability at 14%.

As the petitioner is a minor and due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner is having difficulty to walk for long time and do his dayto day M.V.C.No.5430/2022 17 SCCH - 7 work due to which in his future life the petitioner may suffer from disability.

16. Further in the authority reported in (2014) 14 SCC 396 in between Mallikarjun V/s Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Ltd., and Another wherein it is held that in case of a non earning member, i.e., minor if disability is 10% and up to 30% to the whole body Rs.3,00,000/, up to 60% Rs.4,00,000/, up to 90% Rs.5,00,000/ and above 90% it should be Rs.6,00,000/ and for permanent disability up to 10% it should be Rs.1,00,000/ unless there are exceptional circumstances to take a different yardstick.

entities.text: Mallikarjun V/s Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Ltd., and Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case on hand the treated doctor has assessed total permanent disability at 14%.
In this case as per the evidence of doctor goes to show that the petitioner is having permanent physical disability to an extent of 14%.

By relying on the above said authority I am M.V.C.No.5430/2022 18 SCCH - 7 of the considered view that the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,00,000/ under the head of pain and suffering already undergone and to be suffered in future, mental and physical shock, hardship, inconvenience, and discomforts etc., and loss of amenities in life on account of permanent disability.

Further due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner was admitted in the hospital from 17.09.2022 to 28.09.200 for treatment for 12 days and again he was admitted in the hospital from 11.10.2022 to 13.10.2022 for 4 days.
Hence during this period the his parents have attended the hospital and they have lost some earnings due to the hospitalization of the petitioner for the injuries sustained in the accident.
Hence an amount of Rs.25,000/ is awarded under the head of discomfort, inconvenience and loss of earnings to the parents during the period of hospitalization.
Further PW.1 has produced the hospital and medicine bills as per Ex.P.18 for an M.V.C.No.5430/2022 19 SCCH - 7 amount of Rs.1,07,732/.
Hence an amount of Rs.1,07,732/ is awarded under the head of medical and incidental expenses during the period of hospitalization.

sentences.text:
Towards Hospital and medicine Rs.
1,07,732.00 charges Total Rs. 4,32,732.00 Hence the petitioner is entitled for just and reasonable compensation amount of Rs.4,32,732/.
17.

While answering issue No.1 this tribunal come to conclusion that this accident was occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the BMTC Car bearing M.V.C.No.5430/2022 20 SCCH - 7 registration No.KA01FA1111.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and the respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said Car.
The respondent No.2 admitted that as on the date of the accident the policy issued to the BMTC Car bearing registration No.KA01FA1111 was in force.

Hence the respondent No.1 has not violated the terms and conditions of the Insurance Policy as such the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurer of the above said BMTC Car bearing registration No.KA01FA1111 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization of the entire amount.
Hence I answered the issue No.3 in partly affirmative.
18. Issue No.4:

Petitioners are awarded just and  reasonable compensation of Rs.4,32,732/
(Rupees Four lakhs Thirty Two Thousand Seven Hundred and Thirty Two Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition to till the date of depositing of the compensation amount in the court.

The respondent No.2 is the insurer of the BMTC Car bearing registration No.KA01 FA 1111 is directed to deposit the awarded compensation amount to the petitioner in the court within 02 month from the date of this judgment.
Draw award accordingly.
